verdict: Visa's net revenue rose 12% to $10.7B as payments volume grew 9% and cross-border volume 12% — but a $903M litigation provision cut GAAP profit 4% to $5.1B, even as underlying EPS rose 10%.

segments.name: Service revenue
segments.note: Fees from banks for using the Visa brand and network on cards — based on the prior quarter's payments volume.

segments.name: Data processing revenue
segments.note: Fees for clearing and processing each transaction — processed transactions grew 10%.

segments.name: International transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees when a card is used outside its home country — cross-border volume rose 12% in constant dollars.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Value-added services — fraud tools, data and consulting for banks and merchants.

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Pay and benefits for Visa's workforce.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

opex.name: Litigation provision
opex.note: Almost entirely the special item for the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) case and other uncovered legal matters — a legal charge Visa excludes from its non-GAAP results.

opex.name: Network, professional & depreciation
opex.note: Network and processing ($239M), professional fees ($256M) and depreciation & amortization ($316M).

follow100Note: Per $100 of gross revenue (before client incentives). Measured against Visa's reported net revenue of $10.7B instead, the kept profit is $47.46 per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Volume growth stayed strong
takeaways.text: Net revenue rose 12% to $10.7B — data processing +17%, other revenue +21%, service revenue +10% and international transactions +10%. Payments volume grew 9% in constant dollars, cross-border volume 12% and processed transactions 10%.

takeaways.title: Underlying EPS rose 10%
takeaways.text: Non-GAAP EPS was $2.98, up 10%, and non-GAAP net income $5.8B, up 7%. GAAP EPS slipped 1% to $2.62 because of the legal charge below. Visa also raised its quarterly dividend 14% to $0.67 a share.

takeaways.title: The legal bill spiked again
takeaways.text: The litigation provision was $903M — mostly a $899M special item for the interchange MDL case and other uncovered legal matters, vs just $10M a year ago. It cut GAAP net income 4% to $5.1B; Visa excludes it from non-GAAP results.

oneTimers: A litigation provision of $903M sits in operating expenses, $899M of it the special item for the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) case and other uncovered legal matters; Visa excludes it from non-GAAP results.

Also excluded from non-GAAP results: $54M of amortization of acquired intangible assets and $12M of acquisition-related costs, and $46M of net gains on equity investments. Non-GAAP net income was $5.8B ($2.98 per share).
otherDetail: Investment income and other gains of $285M, less $210M of interest expense — net +$75M.
footerNote: Visa reports 'net revenue' of $10,724M; this page starts from gross revenue of $14,972M so the $4,248M of client incentives shows as a cost.
